title: Work & study
goal: Talk about jobs, school and university, and say what you can, can't, must and don't have to do.
intro:
'What do you do?' — **के काम गर्नुहुन्छ?** — is one of the first questions Nepalis ask, often followed by questions about your salary. In this unit you'll learn words for jobs and education, and three of the most useful verb patterns in the language:

**-न सक्छु** 'I can', **-न आउँछ** 'I know how to', and **-नुपर्छ** 'I have to'.

vocab.note: Especially a salaried job. जागिर खानु 'to have a job' (lit. eat a job!).
f शिक्षिका. Pupils call teachers सर / मिस.
Formal: विद्यालय. Private English-medium schools are called बोर्डिङ स्कुल.
Colloquially also जाँच. परीक्षा दिनु 'to sit an exam'.

vocab.en: to be able, can; to finish
vocab.note: बोल्न सक्छु 'I can speak'; काम सक्यो 'the work is finished'.

vocab.en: to have to; to fall; to cost; to lie (location)
vocab.note: जानुपर्छ 'have to go'; पानी पर्छ 'it rains'; कति पर्छ? 'how much?'

vocab.en: to get, receive; to be allowed to
vocab.note: जान पाउँछु? 'may I go?'; यहाँ फोटो खिच्न पाइन्छ? 'can one take photos here?'

phrases.native: म शिक्षक हुँ। म स्कुलमा पढाउँछु।
phrases.roman: ma sikchhak huṃ. ma skulmā paḍhāuṃchhu.
phrases.en: I'm a teacher. I teach at a school.
I have an exam tomorrow; I have to study.
I don't have to go to the office today.
I know how to use a computer.
Is it OK to take photos here?

grammar.title: Can, know how to, may: सक्नु, आउनु, पाउनु
grammar.body:
All three take the verb in its **-न** form (stem + न: गर्न, बोल्न, खान, जान).

**-न सक्नु** — 'can, be able to' (ability or circumstance):
म नेपाली बोल्न **सक्छु** 'I can speak Nepali'. Negative **सक्दिनँ**, polite **सक्नुहुन्छ?**

**-न आउनु** — 'know how to' (a learned skill), experiencer pattern:
**मलाई** पौडी खेल्न **आउँछ** 'I know how to swim'; मलाई गाडी चलाउन आउँदैन 'I can't drive'.

**-न पाउनु** — 'get to, be allowed to':
म भोलि जान **पाउँछु**? 'May I go tomorrow?' The impersonal **पाइन्छ** asks 'is it allowed?': भित्र जुत्ता लगाएर जान पाइँदैन 'you're not allowed in with shoes'.

Note: सक्नु on its own also means 'to finish': खाना सक्यो 'the food is finished', काम सकेँ 'I finished the work'.

examples.en: You're not allowed to take photos inside the temple.

grammar.title: Must and have to: -नुपर्छ
grammar.body:
**Verb-नु + पर्छ** = 'must, have to' (lit. 'it falls to do'). It does not change for the person; the person can be shown with **-ले** (most common with transitive verbs), **-लाई**, or just the plain pronoun:

म/मैले काम **गर्नुपर्छ** 'I have to work'
मलाई अस्पताल **जानुपर्छ** 'I have to go to hospital'

**Past**: **-नुपर्‍यो** 'had to' — हिजो मैले ढिलोसम्म काम गर्नुपर्‍यो.
**Don't have to**: **-नुपर्दैन** — आज स्कुल जानुपर्दैन 'no school today'.
**Mustn't**: **-नुहुँदैन** (unit 9) — that's a prohibition, not just 'no need'.

Also very common: **-नु छ** 'I've got to (I have this to do)': मलाई बजार जानु छ 'I've got to go to the market'.

examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.
Students have to wear a uniform.
Yesterday I had to work overtime.
I've got to go to the office now.

dialogue.title: Exam season
dialogue.setting: Sarah chats with Kabita, her neighbour's teenage daughter, who is studying on the roof terrace.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Kabita, which class are you in?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: What do you want to do later?

lines.speaker: Kabita
lines.native: म नर्स बन्न चाहन्छु। तर त्यसका लागि धेरै पढ्नुपर्छ।
lines.roman: ma nars banna chāhanchhu. tara tyaskā lāgi dherai paḍhnuparchha.
lines.en: I want to become a nurse. But for that I have to study a lot.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Do you have exams now too?

lines.speaker: Kabita
lines.native: हो, अर्को महिना। दिनको आठ घण्टा पढ्नुपर्छ।
lines.roman: ho, arko mahinā. dinko āṭh ghanṭā paḍhnuparchha.
lines.en: Yes, next month. I have to study eight hours a day.

lines.speaker: Kabita
lines.native: अलिअलि सक्छु, तर बोल्न लाज लाग्छ।
lines.roman: aliali sakchhu, tara bolna lāj lāgchha.
lines.en: A little, but I'm shy to speak it.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: लाज नमान! म तिमीलाई सिकाउन सक्छु।
lines.roman: lāj namāna! ma timilāi sikāuna sakchhu.
lines.en: Don't be shy! I can teach you.

lines.speaker: Kabita
lines.native: साँच्चै? धन्यवाद दिदी! बदलामा म तपाईंलाई नेपाली सिकाउँछु।
lines.roman: sāṃchchai? dhanyabād didi! badalāmā ma tapāiṃlāi nepāli sikāuṃchhu.
lines.en: Really? Thank you, didi! In return I'll teach you Nepali.

culture: Education is a huge family investment in Nepal. The **SEE** exam at the end of class 10 is a major milestone, followed by '+2' (classes 11–12) at a कलेज. Many families pay for private English-medium 'boarding schools'. A secure government job (सरकारी जागिर), won through the competitive **लोक सेवा** exams, carries great prestige. At the same time, millions of Nepalis work abroad — in the Gulf, Malaysia, Korea, Japan and beyond — and the money they send home (रेमिट्यान्स) is a pillar of the economy; almost every family has someone **विदेशमा** 'abroad'.

tip.title: Saying your job
tip.body:
- Your job is **who you are**, so use हो: म नर्स **हुँ**, ऊ ड्राइभर **हो**, हामी किसान **हौँ**.
- Respectful: बुबा किसान **हुनुहुन्छ**.
- To ask: तपाईं **के काम गर्नुहुन्छ?** 'what work do you do?'
tip.pattern: म + job + हुँ  ·  उहाँ + job + हुनुहुन्छ

sentences.en: I'm an engineer.
My father is a farmer.
My aunt is a nurse.
He's a driver.
Are you a teacher?
No, I'm a businessman.
We're farmers.
What does your brother do?
I don't have a job right now.

sentences.native: म बिहान नौ बजे अफिस जान्छु।
sentences.roman: ma bihāna nau baje aphis jānchhu.
sentences.en: I go to the office at nine in the morning.
My boss is a nice person.
There's a meeting at two today.
Where is your company?
The salary is good in this job.
I have the day off tomorrow.
The boss is in a meeting.
My computer isn't working.
The office is closed on Saturdays.

lessons.title: School and university
new: म शिक्षक हुँ। म स्कुलमा पढाउँछु।

sentences.en: What year is your little brother in?
My little sister studies at college.
I teach English.

sentences.native: यो विश्वविद्यालयमा धेरै विदेशी विद्यार्थी छन्।
sentences.roman: yo biswabidyālayamā dherai bidesi bidyārthi chhan.
sentences.en: There are lots of foreign students at this university.
What time does school open?
This book is very good.
There's a lot of homework today.
My mother teaches at a school.
The students are in class.

tip.title: -नुपर्छ — have to
tip.body:
- Verb **-नु + पर्छ** = 'have to' (lit. 'it falls to do'). It never changes for the person: म/तपाईं/ऊ जा**नुपर्छ**.
- The doer often takes **-ले**: **मैले** काम गर्नुपर्छ.
- 'Had to': **-नुपर्‍यो**. 'Don't have to': **-नुपर्दैन**.

sentences.en: I have to do a lot of work today.
Students have to bring a pen to the exam.
There's no school tomorrow. (lit. don't have to go)
I have to buy a new notebook.

sentences.native: हिजो मैले राति एघार बजेसम्म काम गर्नुपर्‍यो।
sentences.roman: hijo maile rāti eghāra bajesamma kām garnuparyo.
sentences.en: Yesterday I had to work until eleven at night.
You don't need to bring anything.
I have to go home now.
You need to study hard. (to a friend)
What day is the exam?
Where's my pen?

tip.title: सक्नु, आउनु, पाउनु
tip.body:
- All three follow the **-न** form of a verb: बोल्**न**, जा**न**, पकाउ**न**.
- **-न सक्छु** 'I can': म आउन सक्छु. Not: **सक्दिनँ**.
- A learned skill: **मलाई** … **-न आउँछ** 'I know how to'.
- Permission: **-न पाउँछु?** 'may I?'; **पाइन्छ?** 'is it allowed?'
tip.pattern: म + verb-न + सक्छु  ·  मलाई + verb-न + आउँछ

sentences.en: I can speak a little Nepali.
I can't go to the meeting today.
Can you come tomorrow?
Can you use a computer? (to a friend)
I know how to cook.
He can't speak English.
May I take tomorrow off?
You're not allowed to take meat into the temple.
I'm learning Nepali.
Is it hard to learn a new language?

sentences.native: मेरो काम सक्यो, अब घर जान्छु।
sentences.roman: mero kām sakyo, aba ghar jānchhu.
sentences.en: My work's done, now I'm going home.
